typical_time: Labs in the post-sleep period before eating or drinking (see fasting labs row)
who: Two crew members examine each other; results go to the flight surgeon
device: Medical computer plus vitals kit (BP cuff, thermometer, pulse oximeter, peak flow meter, stethoscope, otoscope)
steps_plain: Get the exam kit. Take vital signs first. Answer the health questions. Do the body check with your crewmate. Save the results for the flight surgeon.
quote: Periodic Health Status (PHS) examinations requires crew members to perform these exams on each other monthly.

frequency: Monthly in PHS; more often if ill
device: Automatic BP cuff shows pulse; pulse oximeter also shows pulse
steps_plain: Rest quietly first. Read the pulse from the BP cuff or pulse oximeter. Write it down.
quote: Blood pressure and pulse rate are alternatively displayed every 2 seconds.

frequency: Monthly in PHS; every 5 min in emergencies per checklist
steps_plain: Plug the hose into the cuff unit. Wrap the cuff on your bare upper arm with the tube on the inside. Keep the lower edge about 2.5 cm above the elbow bend. Press POWER and wait for 0. Press START. Hold still until the beep. Write down both numbers. If no reading, press SELECT and try again.
quote: Lower ABPC edge should be approximately 2.5 cm (1 inch) above natural bend of elbow as shown.

steps_plain: Use a new disposable oral thermometer. Read it in Celsius. Do not measure right after exercise. Write it down.
quote: Oral Disposable Thermometers (P3-A2)

frequency: Monthly in PHS; every 5 min in emergencies
steps_plain: Put the pulse oximeter on a finger. Press ON. Wait for a steady number. Write down oxygen and pulse.
quote: Attach Pulse Oximeter (Assessment-1) to finger.

frequency: During PHS with blood labs (interval NOT FOUND)
typical_time: After waking, before eating or drinking
device: Blood analyzer and urine strips (2001 list: PCBA, Reflotron, Chemstrip)
steps_plain: Do this right after waking. Do not eat or drink first. Follow the lab card. Record the results.
quote: Laboratory studies, including Blood Chemistry and Urinalysis, must be done in the post-sleep period prior to eating or drinking.

item: Private Medical Conference (PMC) with flight surgeon
who: One crew member and the crew surgeon, private
steps_plain: Go to a private spot. Talk with your flight surgeon. Report any symptoms or medicines taken.
quote: The crewmember additionally has weekly private medical conferences (PMC) with the crew surgeon.

who: Crew member with a psychiatrist or clinical psychologist
steps_plain: Go to a private spot. Talk with the psychologist. Share how you feel and how the team is doing.
quote: crewmembers do have regular Private Psychological Conferences (PPC) with a psychiatrist or clinical psychologist

frequency: Monthly in orbit; also after any unexpected medical event
steps_plain: Open the test on the laptop. Do all the tasks. Compare with your own baseline. Tell the surgeon if the score is off.
quote: WinSCAT (Space flight Cognitive Assessment Tool for Windows), which is an 11- to 15-minute computer-based cognitive screening test

steps_plain: Do your scheduled exercise. Log the device and minutes.
quote: 2.5hrs exercise daily

device: ARED (resistive), T2 treadmill and CEVIS cycle (aerobic)
steps_plain: Do resistive exercise on ARED. Do aerobic exercise on the treadmill or bike. Log minutes for each.
quote: with crew members now averaging two hours of exercise per day

steps_plain: Go to your crew quarters at the planned time. Log how many hours you slept when you wake.
quote: 8.5hrs rest daily

frequency: Daily during set weeks (e.g. one week in every three, research protocol)
steps_plain: After you wake, log sleep time, sleep quality and any sleep medicine.
quote: were scheduled to complete it on a daily basis during specified intervals (e.g., one week out of every three weeks)

steps_plain: Wear your dosimeter. Look at the screen. Note total dose and dose rate.
quote: the always-on display provides the astronaut with their total mission dose and the recently measured dose rate at a glance

steps_plain: Use the mass device as trained. Record your mass in kg.
quote: After an initial loss in the first 30 d of flight, body mass remained constant through the rest of the mission

device: Computer questionnaire (later iPad Food Intake Tracker)
steps_plain: Once a week, fill in what you usually ate.
quote: a Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ) (Figure 10; Figure 11) was designed with the goal of having crews report typical intake once per week

steps_plain: Take your vitamin D as your flight surgeon told you. Tick it off.
quote: In 2006, vitamin D recommendations to crews increased from 400 IU vitamin D/d to 800 IU vitamin D /d.

steps_plain: List every medicine you took since the last check.
quote: Complete Medical History section. List Medications taken.

device: Near and far acuity, Amsler grid, contrast sensitivity charts
steps_plain: Do the eye chart test as trained. Record any change in near or far vision.
quote: Vision Testing (Near, Far Acuity, Amsler Grid, Contrast Sensitivity)
